html:
Lamanai is a Maya site on the New River Lagoon in northern Belize, lived in for some three thousand years, from before 1000 BCE into the 1600s. Its name means "submerged crocodile".

Unlike most Maya cities of the region, Lamanai was not deserted in the Classic collapse. It went on trading and building through the Postclassic centuries, so it shows how Maya life carried on after the great southern cities fell.

Spanish friars came in the 1500s and built churches beside the old temples. The people later rose against Spanish rule and burned a church, and the town faded. Its Mask Temple and High Temple are among the best-known ruins in Belize, linked to Maya history from the first villages to the conquest.
sum: Lamanai is a Maya site on the New River Lagoon in northern Belize, lived in for some three thousand years, from before 1000 BCE into the 1600s. Its name means "submerged crocodile".
